questions: Where is your hometown, and what is it like?
What do you like most about the area where you live?
Has your hometown changed much in recent years?
Would you like to settle there in the future? Why or why not?
Do you work, or are you a student at the moment?
What led you to choose that job or course?
What is the most interesting part of your work or studies?
If you could change one thing about your job or course, what would it be?
How much of your day do you spend using technology?
Is there any piece of technology you would find hard to live without?
Do you ever feel you spend too much time looking at screens?
Have you learned to use any new technology recently?

part2.cue_card: Describe a public place in your area that you think is well designed.
prompts: Where this place is and what it looks like
What makes it pleasant or easy to spend time in
How often you go there and why
follow_ups: Has this place changed since you first started going there?
Do you think your area needs more places like this?

questions: Why do you think some public spaces attract far more people than others?
Should a city keep land as a park or square when it could be sold for housing?
Do you agree that thoughtful design can reduce crime and antisocial behaviour in public places?
How has the way people spend time together in public changed over the past few decades?
Are privately owned spaces, such as shopping centres, as valuable to a community as genuinely public ones?
What role should local residents play in deciding how a public space is designed and used?
